title: Shell programming
subtitle: Scripts, xtrace, and environment vs shell variables

cards.meaning: Text file the shell interprets line by line (not a precompiled binary)
cards.notes: Memory hook: script = recipe the cook reads as it goes. Compiled program = meal already cooked.

cards.meaning: Run the script with xtrace for the whole process (no file edit)
cards.notes: Each command prints to stderr with a + (PS4) after expansions. Same idea: bash -x -c 'echo "$HOME"'.

cards.meaning: Turn xtrace on from this line (script or prompt)
cards.notes: Long name: set -o xtrace. Scope is from here until set +x or the end.

cards.example: set -x; echo traced; set +x; echo quiet
cards.notes: Minus = option on, plus = option off. Wrap a block you care about, leave quiet elsewhere.

cards.meaning: Assign a variable — no spaces around =
cards.notes: KEY = value is wrong (shell treats KEY as a command). Names are case-sensitive.

cards.meaning: Multiple values in one variable, separated by :
cards.notes: How PATH works. First matching executable in order wins.

cards.meaning: Environment is inherited by children; shell-only stays in this shell until exported
cards.notes: Memory hook: environment = inherited by kids. Shell-only = stays in the room.

cards.meaning: Print the home directory of the current user
cards.notes: Quote expansions. HOME is a common environment variable.

cards.meaning: Colon-separated directories searched for commands; first match wins
cards.notes: Put ~/bin at the front to override /usr/bin. Walked in order when you type ls, python, …
Contrast with set — set also prints shell vars and functions (huge).
Noisy. Use env/printenv when you only want exported environment.

cards.meaning: Logged-in user / default editor / login shell path / locale
cards.notes: Also LOGNAME, TERM, MAIL. Convention: UPPER_CASE with _ between words.
